subject: OmniCloud private deploy: architecture readout & egress clarity

Subject: OmniCloud private deploy — initial architecture pass and questions

Rachel / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. OmniCloud is moving to a VPC-isolated Redwood Private deployment for our inference workloads and the infra team asked for a short architecture readout so they can sanity-check egress, control/data-plane demarcation, and routing for compliance. We attached the diagram we used in the PoC for context.

Key asks from my side:
- Clear demarc for control plane traffic (auth, heartbeats, admin) vs data plane (inference requests, model artifacts).
- Egress pathways for telemetry and model fetches (we need a list of exact endpoints and ports).
- Any required NAT / proxy components inside the customer VPC vs Redwood-managed components.
- A short checklist for SOC2 / network evidence we should be prepared to show.

Can we do a 45-minute readout today or tomorrow? We have Asha (security lead) + three infra engineers.

Attachments: omnideploy_v1_diagram.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)

Thanks,
Ops Team
OmniCloud Systems

Hi — appreciate the diagram and the clear asks. We're available for a readout today at 3pm PT or tomorrow morning. 45 minutes is perfect.

Quick answers up front so your infra team has something to chew on before the call: 
- Control plane: TLS-authenticated control signals (telemetry, heartbeats, config) flow over dedicated mTLS channels to the Redwood control-plane endpoint in the selected region. Those endpoints are outbound from customer VPC to our control plane (no inbound holes required).
- Data plane: inference requests are handled entirely inside the customer VPC when using the "Private (VPC)" option — runtime sits in your subnet(s) and accepts requests from your application network. Model pulls during deployment are outbound HTTPS to our artifact CDN (we'll list exact hostnames).
- Egress: telemetry and model fetches need outbound access to: artifacts.redwood.ai (443), control.redwood.ai (443), logs.redwood.ai (443), and the STS/KMS endpoints for your cloud provider. We'll provide a full host/port list in the readout doc.
- NAT / proxies: a NAT gateway or egress proxy is required for outbound-only flows from your private subnets. Redwood can operate with either customer-managed proxy (preferred for egress filtering) or a pre-provisioned NAT; we don't require inbound ports.
- Evidence checklist: SOC2-relevant items include: (a) control-plane TLS cert chain and rotation cadence, (b) audit log retention policy (we recommend 90 days by default), (c) packet-level egress allowlist, and (d) deployment manifests for model images. We'll enumerate these in a one-page checklist.

Jonas — adding you for the demarcation notes and to confirm the proposed attachment topology. Marcus FYI for the compliance items.

I'll slot today 15:00 PT and send a calendar with an agenda unless you prefer tomorrow AM.

--

Thanks Rachel — adding a few technical specifics that I want to surface before the readout so we can make the session actionable.

Summary of recommended demarcation (high level):
- Control plane (Redwood-managed endpoints, outbound-only):
  - Components: control.redwood.ai (mTLS), cert-rotation service, rollout API.
  - Traffic: heartbeat pings, rollout commands, health/metrics push.
  - Ports: 443 (TLS) for all control endpoints; we recommend allowing outbound to the FQDNs rather than raw IPs.

- Data plane (customer-hosted within VPC):
  - Components: inference runtime, KV cache, local model cache
  - Traffic: inference API (gRPC or HTTPS depending on your preference), inter-node KV replication (internal CIDR), model fetch (outbound HTTPS to artifacts.redwood.ai)
  - Ports: 443 for model/artifact pulls; 50051 (gRPC) or 443 (HTTPS) for inference API depending on chosen transport.

Attachment and evidence notes (attached):
- controlplane-egress-checklist.xlsx -> concise host/port list + recommended retention windows.
- omnideploy_sequence_notes.txt -> sequence diagram notes for deploy (pull, validate, mount, start) and rollback.

Operational patterns and optional proxy placements:
- Recommended: put a customer-managed egress proxy in a centralized services subnet. All runtime nodes route model/artifact pulls through that proxy so security can apply allowlists and TLS inspection as needed.
- Alternative: use cloud-provider NAT gateway + Security Group rules if your org can't run a proxy. We'll list the tradeoffs in the readout.

Drive link to updated diagram and a proposed annotated topology: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/omnideploy-diagrams-DC-9843

I'll bring the annotated topology to the call and share the one-page SOC2 checklist.

Attachments: controlplane-egress-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 42KB), omnideploy_sequence_notes.txt (text/plain, 3.8KB)

A couple of quick follow-ups before the readout:
- Can you confirm whether control-plane telemetry will include IP-level logs or just aggregate metrics? (we need to know for retention rules)
- For artifact downloads: will the payloads be pulled from a CDN edge with short-lived signed URLs, or from a central artifacts host? Our security policy prefers short-lived signed URLs.

Also please attach the one-page SOC2 checklist and the host/port allowlist to the calendar invite — Miguel will use that to pre-populate our egress firewall rules before the meeting.
